sources.citation: Zwisler, Joshua James. 2021. Indigenous Identity Post-Linguicide: A study among the Pijao of Central Coyaima, Colombia. PhD thesis, Monash University. DOI 10.26180/14446377.v1. 220 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Pijao stress or tone. pp. 17-19: 'Very little is known about the extinct Pijao language'; sources are short vocabulary lists (Simon 1627, Rivet 1943, Loukotka 1963, Durbin & Seijas 1973), Reichel-Dolmatoff's toponymy (200+ entries) and Ramirez Sendoya 1952 (c. 800 words, judged unreliable); p. 19 states no grammatical description was made before the language disappeared. All stress/accent/pitch/syllable hits belong to GAT-2 transcription conventions or the Spanish-ethnolect chapters. Mentions Faust 1986 and a paused community vocabulary project.

sources.citation: Paredes Cisneros, Santiago. 2018. Lengua pijao como lengua franca en las gobernaciones de Popayán y Neiva, siglos XVI-XVII. Fronteras de la Historia 23(1): 40-66. DOI 10.22380/20274688.311.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content. pp. 45-46: 'Si bien existen estudios detallados para lenguas caribe de otras regiones, se carece de información acerca de la estructura de la lengua pijao o, al menos, esos trabajos no la mencionan' and 'Además de las terminaciones, es poco lo que puede colegirse de la estructuración de las palabras o cómo se articulaban.' Discusses recurrent toponymic endings (-ima, -ema, -ma, -me; -arco, -co; -ira; cal-), Carib-affiliation debate, colonial use of Pijao as a lingua franca around Buga/La Plata, and cites Ramírez Sendoya 1952 pp. XXXII-XXXVII, 221-225 and Reichel-Dolmatof…

sources.citation: Zwisler, Joshua James. 2018. The Intergenerational Perception of the Causes and Effects of Language Loss in the Pijao Community of Natagaima, Colombia. Lenguaje 46(2): 220-248. DOI 10.25100/lenguaje.v46i2.6581.

sources.citation: Zwisler, Joshua James. 2018. The Pijao of Natagaima: Post-Linguicide Indigenous Identity and Language. Cadernos de Etnolingüística 6(1): 51-80.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §4.3 (pp. 70-72) gives a community-compiled Pijao word list in an orthography 'based on, but not identical, to the system used by Durbin and Seijas (1973) with diacritics representing stress' — stress is marked per item (amé, alamán, çaguála, golúpa, kahírre, hoté, huíl, nuhúgi, tínki, toléma, tenú, óreme..) but no rule is stated. §4.2 describes the Spanish ethnolect of Natagaima (word-final vowel lengthening, 'cantado' clause-final intonation), not the Pijao language.
